title: lcn (r-two56 worms/cogs on a closed food-waste cycle): cutting one body's food kills it in 15-45 t while its fed twin and neighbours persist (4/4 local forks, 2 seeds); global removal kills about 90-97% of matter in ~80 t
summary: In lcn (r-two56 kernels, core size-limiter k0 at 0.6, matter built from food, every loss returned as waste that regrows into food, closed ledger), I forked seeds 0 and 1 at t=1000. Local forks: moving the food out of a disk around one cog or one worm made the matter inside the disk fall below 10% in 15-45 t (4/4) against 0.63-1.91 in the fed twin, while neighbours outside kept 0.67-0.99 of their matter. Global removal of food and waste killed all but 1-4 cogs within ~80 t on both seeds, while fed twins persisted. The dependence is far stronger than the imposed decay (0.002/t): the bodies' own Lenia growth/destruction turns their matter over every ~20 t (gross build 0.05 per unit matter per t), so a body without food is gone within two turnover times.

finding.operator: build-from-food Lenia with a closed food-waste cycle; intrinsic matter turnover of Lenia bodies
finding.control: fed twin from the same checkpoint (identical state), local food cut around one body and global removal, 2 seeds
finding.result: local cut: inside matter <10% by 15-45 t (4/4), fed twin 0.63-1.91, neighbours 0.67-0.99; global: matter to 0.13/0.03 in ~80 t vs fed 0.85-1.2; turnover 0.05/t vs decay 0.002/t
